source_evidence: High-yield.  These bonds have a lower credit rating, implying higher credit risk, than investment-grade bonds and, therefore, offer higher interest rates in return for the increased risk.
question: Misconception: High-yield bonds are a safer, higher-quality kind of bond than investment-grade bonds because they pay more interest.
answer: A higher interest rate does not mean a bond has higher credit quality. According to the source, high-yield bonds have lower credit ratings and higher credit risk than investment-grade bonds; their higher interest rates are offered in return for that increased risk.
